reason: A keeps the product graphic in one piece, but the cream badge is jammed into the top-left corner, almost touching the headline. The NEW pill is as heavy as the Try It CTA, so the two compete. The subhead sits below the buttons, which breaks reading order, and the bottom third is dead space. B breaks the product graphic: the cream circle is pulled off and stranded in the bottom-left corner, and the bottle, now orange on orange, almost disappears into the background. The headline is undersized, the NEW pill floats alone at the top-right, and there are large empty gaps between the copy blocks.

A keeps a clear left-to-right order: brand and headline on the left, then date and a prominent RSVP button in the middle. Its flaws: the pills are spread unevenly along the bottom, the legal text is tiny and crammed right next to the Tastings pill, and the missing-asset placeholder is clipped at the right edge. B buries the CTA: RSVP shrinks into a pill the same size as the tag pills. B also has a jumbled pill row that crowds the headline, a subhead squeezed into a narrow column that wraps over five lines, a gap between the date and time, a 'SOLST CE' wordmark that looks broken, and a decorative dot that collides with the 'Reserve a spot' text.

A has a clean left-to-right banner: the quote, attribution and quote mark share a left edge, and the circle is cropped off the edge as in the original. But the quote text is small for the format, the logo is tiny and indented off the text edge, floating above dead space, and the can sits off-centre toward the top-left of the circle. B gives the quote better size, but there is a big gap between the quote mark and the quote. The attribution wraps to two lines and is jammed into a row with an oversized logo that competes with it. The can sits in the top half of a fully enclosed circle, leaving the lower half empty, so the composition feels less intentional.

A: the headline's left edge (~x125) doesn't line up with the CTA (~x48). The three-line headline is jammed against the top edge and the CTA nearly touches the bottom, and the legal line is squeezed up against the button. The phone sits isolated beyond a large dead gap in the middle. B: a clean left-to-right banner (phone, one-line headline, CTA) that keeps the brand intact, but the CTA is undersized and stranded far right behind a wide empty gap, and the legal text is shrunk to near-illegible size.

A breaks the product graphic. The cream circle is split off into the bottom-left corner as a leftover blob, and the can is now an orange outline on an orange background, so it almost disappears. The headline is too small for the canvas, the NEW pill floats alone in the top right, and the large empty gaps make the layout look scattered. B keeps the can-in-circle logo intact and the text is readable, but it is cramped: the circle is jammed into the top-left corner and almost touches the headline, which runs nearly to the right edge. The NEW and Try It buttons are oversized and compete with the headline, the subline sits under the buttons so the reading order is wrong, and the bottom third is empty.

A shrinks the RSVP CTA into a small pill that looks like just another badge, so the call to action is buried. The italic subhead is squeezed into a narrow four-line column wedged between the headline and the date. The logo reads 'SOLST CE', the legal text is tiny, and the missing-asset box is still visible. B keeps the one-line headline and a prominent RSVP button, and its reading order is clear. However, the badges sit jammed against the bottom edge, the illegibly small fine print is crammed next to them, the missing-asset placeholder is cut off at the right edge, and the can floats alone in a mostly empty right side.

A: the jar sits in the upper half of a fully enclosed circle, leaving the bottom of the circle empty, so the circle no longer bleeds off the corner as in the original. The logo is blown up and set beside the attribution, where it competes with it and breaks the original's stacked order, and a large gap separates the quote mark from the quote. B: it keeps the original's structure (quote mark, quote, attribution and logo stacked on the left, with the jar centred in a circle that bleeds off the bottom-right) with clean left alignment. Its flaws are minor: the logo wordmark is very small and the jar is a bit small for the canvas.

A uses a sensible left-to-right banner flow (phone, one-line headline, CTA). However, the headline is undersized for the canvas, the '7 days free' fine print is tiny and hard to read, and a large dead gap separates the copy from the small CTA pinned to the far right. B keeps the 3-line stacked headline from the square original, so it looks shrunk rather than rearranged for the banner. Its CTA sits off the headline's left edge and is jammed against the bottom of the canvas with the fine print crammed beside it, and the headline crowds the top edge while the middle of the banner is empty.

A uses a left-to-right banner layout that fits the format, but the headline is jammed against the right column: the period in 'sunshine.' nearly touches the CTA, and the 'Solstice…' copy breaks into four ragged centred lines ending in the orphan 'flavours.' B is a clean but mostly shrunk copy of the original stack, with tight top and bottom margins, wide empty sides and supporting copy too small to read comfortably. Even so, it keeps the hierarchy and spacing more orderly and has no near-collision.

A keeps the original's centred stack (headline, then subline, then pill CTA) and reads cleanly. Its flaws: the headline is set very large and crowds the top edge, the subline 'Now in four flavours.' is tiny (about 8px), and the three-line wrap breaks awkwardly with 'Bubbles,' alone on line one and 'and a' trailing at the end of line two. B is worse: it wraps the headline to four lines with 'a little' stranded as a short line, and it breaks the centred axis by putting a tiny left-aligned subline beside a right-aligned button on a cramped bottom row. That row sits close to the bottom and side edges and drifts from the original's composition.

A scatters the flavour pills out of order (Honey Rosemary first, Cucumber Mint off to the right on the pink circle, Blood Orange stranded below), squeezes the subtitle into a narrow three-line column beside the CTA, and crowds the lower half. B keeps the headline → subtitle → CTA reading order and the pill sequence, but the pills are as heavy as the CTA and compete with it, the subtitle is tiny, and the off-centre CTA with the staggered pill rows gives an uneven, bottom-heavy grid.

A jams everything into the middle and leaves about 140px of dead space at the bottom. Its left edges don't line up: the headline starts at x≈27 but the subhead starts at x≈10. The three flavour pills are staggered at different x offsets, which looks arbitrary, and the circles bunch up decoratively at the top. B uses the tall format better, with a large, dominant headline and a clear CTA. Its flaws: the logo is centred while the headline and copy are left-aligned, there's an oversized gap between the headline and subhead, the pills run in reverse order to the original and differ in width, and the bottom circle crowds the legal text.

A keeps the reading order and grouping: headline, subcopy and fine print sit in one column, with the CTA next to it and the product plus purple circle on the right. Its flaws: the column is centred instead of the original's left alignment, the oversized CTA competes with the headline, the fine print sits tight to the bottom edge, and the circle is clipped at the top-right edge. B breaks the design into scattered pieces. '20% off' sits inside a circle that is cut off at the bottom-left, 'Every mixed case.' floats away from the headline, and the fine print is stranded on the far right. The order jumps from badge to subcopy to CTA and then back to the headline, so there is no grid or clear hierarchy.

A keeps the original's centred stack and hierarchy intact, but it is mostly a shrink: the headline sits only about 15 px from the top edge, the CTA crowds the bottom, and the subhead is small for the banner. B does reflow left to right, but the headline runs almost into the right column, with 'sunshine.' nearly touching the CTA button. Its subhead is squeezed into a narrow, centred, ragged block ('Now in four / flavours.'), and the right column is jammed against the canvas edge.

A breaks the original's centred stack. The 4-line headline is so big it crowds the top edge, and the tagline and CTA are pushed into a cramped bottom row with almost no bottom margin. The tiny left-aligned tagline looks like a stray caption next to the button. B keeps the centred headline, tagline and CTA hierarchy, but the tagline is very small and jammed right under the headline. The bottom gap is also noticeably bigger than the top, so the stack sits a little high.

A keeps the brand → headline → subhead → CTA order, but the flavour pills are blown up to compete with the CTA. They sit in a ragged, staggered cluster: Cucumber Mint juts against the left edge and the bottom row is jammed at the canvas bottom, which leaves dead space on the left. B has a strong headline, but its right edge nearly touches the canvas. The subhead is squeezed into a narrow 3-line column, and the pills are scattered and out of order (Honey Rosemary, Cucumber Mint, Blood Orange) with no shared alignment. Its lower half reads as random fragments around the CTA.

A uses the full height with a strong headline and CTA, but the centered logo clashes with the left-aligned headline, there is a large dead gap between headline and subcopy, and the flavour pills are reversed from the original order and sit at ragged, inconsistent widths and offsets. B packs everything into the top three-quarters and leaves about 150px of empty space at the bottom. Its headline (x≈27) and subcopy/CTA (x≈10) don't share a left edge, the pills form an uneven staircase, and the headline is small and set over overlapping circles.

A breaks the design into scattered pieces. The headline '20% off' sits in a circle that is cut off at the bottom left, 'Every mixed case' and the CTA float far away along the top, and the fine print sits alone on the right, so there is no reading order or grouping. B keeps the headline, subcopy and fine print together in one centred block, with the CTA next to it and the product on its circle at the right, which is a sensible left-to-right banner. Its flaws: the CTA pill is oversized and competes with the headline, the fine print is jammed near the bottom edge, and the centred text column does not line up with the CTA or the product.

A: the bottom-right row is jammed. The '25% off on June 21.' subhead wraps awkwardly next to the CTA, and the legal text is set almost as large as the subhead, so it competes for attention and sits right against the right edge. The phone runs into the top edge, and the cropped circles behind the logo look accidental. B has a cleaner hierarchy, reading from headline to subhead to CTA, but it still has flaws. The logo is shrunk to near-illegibility, there is dead space between the subhead and the CTA, the legal line is unreadably tiny, and the right circle crowds the CTA.

A keeps the original's centred stack and clear headline > subhead > CTA order. Its flaws are small: the headline is pushed high, leaving a top margin smaller than the bottom one, and the subhead wraps awkwardly, leaving 'four flavours.' alone on its second line. B blows the headline up so far that the subhead and CTA get squeezed into a cramped bottom row. That row has centre-aligned three-line copy sitting next to a button with no shared edge or axis, it sits close to the bottom edge, and it breaks the original's centred top-to-bottom reading order.

A keeps a clean left text column with the right reading order, but the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow is indented about 17px past the left edge of the headline, body and CTA. The middle third is dead space between the text and the can, and the CTA sits tight under the body copy. B breaks the design into scattered pieces: the headline drops below and left of its own body copy, the body copy and CTA float in the centre on a separate axis, and the legal line is shrunk to illegible micro-text under the circle, so the reading order and grouping fall apart.

A: 'Every mixed case.' is squeezed into a narrow column and wraps awkwardly onto three lines next to the CTA. The legal line is crammed under the button and too small to read, and the shoe sits low and off-centre in a large empty circle, so the bottom is jammed while the middle is dead space. B: the order reads correctly (headline, subhead, shoe, CTA) and all text is legible, but the shoe is placed arbitrarily on the circle's edge and there is a large empty band between the CTA and the legal text, so spacing is uneven and needs fixing.

A shrinks the headline into a cramped three-line stack only a few pixels tall and bunches logo, headline, the tiny 'Full review inside.', the tilted badge and the product into the left two-thirds, leaving the right third empty. The fine print and badge are barely readable at this size. B sets the headline on one large line that clearly leads and fills the banner left to right, so it fits the format much better. But 'Full review inside.' sits on top of the green circle's edge (an unwanted collision), the circle touches the top and bottom of the canvas, and the NEW VIDEO badge is wedged under the logo, which looks like an afterthought.

A is the portrait layout pushed into the wide frame. The headline and CTA are crammed down the left side, the CTA almost touches the bottom edge, and the phone is jammed against the right edge. That leaves a large dead gap in the middle, and the fine print sits squashed beside the button. B reads properly left to right (headline → phone → CTA) with balanced weight. Its flaws: the fine print drifts far below the CTA, ungrouped and misaligned with it, and the headline is shrunk so it barely outweighs the button.

A has a clean left-to-right flow: logo and sale ribbon, then the phone, then the headline, subhead and CTA stacked in the right column. However, the phone runs almost to the top and bottom edges, the logo is tiny, and the legal line is jammed under the CTA and is too small to read. B's bottom row is badly cramped: the subhead wraps into an awkward two-line '25% off on / June 21.', and the four-line legal block, almost as prominent as the subhead, is pressed against the right edge. On top of that, the sale ribbon is cropped at the left edge and the decorative circles clutter the top-left corner beside the logo.

A: the headline is oversized and pushes the subcopy and CTA into a cramped side-by-side row near the bottom edge. That breaks the original's centred vertical reading order. The centred three-line subcopy block doesn't line up with the headline axis or the button, and there is extra empty space above the headline. B: keeps the original's centred stack (headline, then subcopy, then CTA) with clear hierarchy and even spacing. The flaws are minor: the subcopy breaks awkwardly ('Now in / four flavours.'), and the bottom margin is slightly heavier than the top.

A breaks the layout into scattered pieces: '20% off' sits far below its eyebrow, and the body copy floats mid-canvas above and to the right of the headline, so it reads in the wrong order. The CTA is on its own random axis, and the legal line is shrunk to illegible micro-text under the circle. B keeps a clean left column (eyebrow, headline, copy, CTA, legal) with the can and circle on the right, which suits a banner. Its flaws are small: 'WEEKEND ONLY' is indented about 17 px past the column's left edge, the CTA sits tight under the copy, and the circle is cropped at the right and bottom edges.

A keeps a clear top-to-bottom order (headline, subhead, shoe, CTA), but the subhead floats in a gap inside the circle and there is a large dead band between the CTA and the legal line. B's subhead 'Every mixed case.' is squeezed into three short lines next to the CTA. Its legal text is shrunk to an unreadable micro-size and pushed against the bottom edge, and the bottom strip is cramped while the area around the circle is underused.

A rearranges the design properly for the banner. The headline sits on one large line and dominates, and it reads left to right from the logo to the product. A uses a proper left-to-right banner flow (headline, phone, CTA) with good legibility, but the legal line hangs far below the CTA with a large gap and isn't aligned to the button's edges, and the headline sits lower than the CTA, so the composition loses its rhythm. B keeps the portrait stacking: the headline wraps to three lines in a wide format, the CTA nearly touches the bottom edge, the legal text is jammed against the button, the phone nearly touches the top and bottom edges, and the middle of the canvas is a large dead area, so it looks crammed and lopsided.

A keeps the headline on one line and reads left to right, but the 'Find a Store' pill is jammed against the top and right canvas edges. It also shrinks the legal text under the CTA to an illegible ~5px block, and the logo and can are cramped in a narrow stacked column. A is the less broken of the two.

A keeps the original reading order (eyebrow, headline, body, CTA, legal), but the dark header band is cut off at the left half. The orange divider is stranded on the far right, the body copy and CTA drift right of the headline's axis in a diagonal stagger, and the right third of the canvas is dead space. It also leaves the logo block and divider isolated, shrinks the CTA until it is weaker than the body copy, splits 'Ships late June' away from the button, and crams the legal text into an unreadable narrow column.

A turns the design into a proper left-to-right banner with a strong headline, but the gap between the end of 'sunshine.' and the CTA pill is almost nothing. The subtext column is also squeezed into four centred lines that break badly ('Now in four / flavours.'), and that column hugs the right edge. B is a clean but shrunk copy of the original stack: the headline sits jammed near the top edge, the subtext is tiny at this size, the CTA nearly touches the bottom, and wide empty bands sit on both sides. A's headline is so large it crowds the canvas, and the CTA is left-aligned under a centred headline. The LIMITED badge is moved to the far right, separate from the button and in a different order than the original, and the bottom group sits tight to the edge. B keeps the original structure: centred headline with the badge next to the CTA. A: the headline is strong, but the RSVP CTA has shrunk to a pill the same size as the FREE ENTRY badge, so the main action is lost among the badges in a 2x2 cluster. A reads left to right as a banner should (brand+can, headline, CTA), but the headline wraps and leaves 'fizz' alone on the second line, the can is shrunk to a speck, and the legal text squeezed under the CTA is illegible. A strands the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow at the bottom left, far below the headline it introduces, and leaves the orange divider floating under the dark logo panel. B keeps a sensible top-to-bottom order (eyebrow, headline, body, CTA, legal), but the headline sits in a left column while the body and CTA are centred on a different axis to the right. B also leaves the divider stranded at the right, the half-width dark band and empty upper right look unfinished, and its legal text is unreadably small. B is the less broken of the two.

A is just the original shrunk into the middle of the strip, not rearranged. The headline sits almost against the top edge, the subcopy is tiny, the button is crammed under it, and both sides are left as wide empty orange bands. B rearranges the design for a wide banner, with the headline large on the left and the copy and button grouped on the right. But 'sunshine.' nearly touches the button, the gutter between the two blocks is too narrow, and the subcopy wraps into a ragged four-line centred block ending in a lone 'flavours.'

A keeps the original structure: the centred headline sits with the LIMITED tag right next to the CTA. However, the badge-plus-button group sits off the headline's centre axis, and a large empty band is left at the bottom. B has a bolder headline, but it breaks the grouping and alignment: the CTA is pushed hard left under a centred headline, the LIMITED tag drifts far right with a big unexplained gap, and the bottom row is cramped near the edge.

A keeps the logo, headline, subtitle and CTA order intact and the RSVP button stays prominent. But the three pills are scattered: TASTINGS floats beside the date, and FREE ENTRY and ALL AGES are split far apart. The legal text is jammed against the URL line at the bottom edge, and the lower-left cluster is cramped.
